race_context: The district: New Prairie United School Corporation is based in New Carlisle {np_form3}. Its board seats are tied to Olive Township (District 1), Hudson and Wills townships (District 2) and Kankakee and Galena townships (District 3) {np_board}. Its schools include Olive Township, Prairie View and Rolling Prairie elementary schools, New Prairie Middle School and New Prairie High School {np_n_260928}. District figures put average 2024-25 enrollment at 2,858 students {np_cps}. Paul White is superintendent {np_admin}{np_n_260928}.

Board and elections: the board has five members, three tied to districts and two at large {np_board}. Current members are Phillip King (president, District 3), Jason DeMeyer (vice president, At Large - District 3), Jill Smith (secretary, At Large - District 1), Rich Shail (District 1) and Rich Gadacz (District 2) {np_board}{np_n_260105}. In 2024, LaPorte County voters filled the District 1 at-large seat (Smith), District 1 (Shail) and District 3 (King) {lp_2024}. The other two seats are on the 2026 ballot.

Seats on the 2026 ballot: the at-large seat for a member from District 2 or District 3, held by DeMeyer, and the District 2 seat, held by Gadacz {in_list}{np_board}. Both incumbents were on the 2022 ballot for these seats {lp_2022_galena1}, and both are running again. DeMeyer faces Eric J. Beebe, and Gadacz is unopposed {in_list}. Each race elects one member {in_list}{np_board}. This guide did not find the district's governing-body plan, so it could not confirm whether all district voters elect the at-large seat.

Budget (2026-2027): at the Aug. 31, 2026 budget hearing, the finance director presented proposed 2027 appropriations: Education Fund $24.3 million, Operations Fund $11.7 million, Referendum Debt Service $5.5 million, Debt Service $1.36 million and Rainy Day $1 million. Board members asked no questions {np_n_260831}. The taxpayer notice estimates $781,900 in property-tax cap credits {np_form3}. The board adopted the 2027 budget, tax rates, capital projects plan and bus replacement plan on Sept. 28, 2026 {np_n_260928}. In June 2026 it approved a resolution transferring money from debt service to the operations fund {np_n_260622}.

Bonds and facilities: at a September 2025 bond hearing, the district's financial consultants presented an option to issue bonds while keeping the existing debt-service tax rate. No members of the public commented then or at the October 2025 hearing {np_n_250917}{np_n_251021}. On Sept. 28, 2026 the board approved an eighth amendment to its building-corporation lease and the issuance of bonds; no one commented at the hearing {np_n_260928}. Projects approved in 2026 include parking-lot work, middle-school flooring, bus purchases and softball and baseball field work {np_ag_260427}{np_n_260622}{np_n_260928}.

Enrollment: the board has repeatedly closed classes to out-of-district transfer students. It closed all K-12 classes through the end of 2025-26, closed some elementary grades and Grade 7 for fall 2026, and on Sept. 28, 2026 closed all schools to new transfer students from Oct. 2, 2026 through the end of the first semester {np_ag_260223}{np_n_260622}{np_n_260803}{np_n_260928}.

Teachers and staff: the board approved the 2025-26 master teacher contract and compensation model in November 2025 {np_n_251111}. At the Sept. 28, 2026 collective-bargaining hearing, a high school science teacher told the board that addressing salary compression by giving veteran teachers smaller raises devalues veteran educators {np_n_260928}. In August 2026 the board raised bus drivers' extracurricular pay from $16 to $18 an hour and added trip and recruitment bonuses {np_n_260831}.

Academics and policy: a March 2026 work session reviewed the district's move to standards-based grading {np_ws_260316}. In September 2026 White and board members praised the district's iLearn results {np_n_260928}. In August 2026 the board moved its policy service from NEOLA to the Indiana School Boards Association {np_n_260824}. King gives legislative reports at meetings, including in 2026 on state bills about student phone use and curriculum mandates {np_n_260129}{np_n_260223}.
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news coverage of these races.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board vice president; listed on the state list as Nonpartisan {np_board}{in_list}.
background: New Prairie High School graduate (2003) with bachelor's degrees in building construction management and civil engineering technology from Purdue University North Central (2008) {np_board}.

President of D.A. Dodd Mechanical, where he has worked since 2008. He serves on the executive board of the St. Joe Valley Mechanical Contractors Association and on the LaPorte County Beef Committee {np_board}.
path_to_ballot: Was on the 2022 ballot for the New Prairie at-large seat {lp_2022_galena1}.
Listed on the state list as Nonpartisan {in_list}.
on_incumbent: Is a current board member; re-elected vice president in January 2026 {np_n_260105}.

In August 2026 he made the motion to approve the meeting agenda and congratulated the FFA program on its students' successes {np_n_260824}. He seconded the motion to close the Aug. 31, 2026 budget hearing {np_n_260831}. He was absent from the March 16 and Sept. 28, 2026 meetings {np_ws_260316}{np_n_260928}.
gaps: No campaign website, questionnaire, forum answers or news coverage of his 2026 campaign found.
Unverified (search snippet only): a summary of the district's board page said he has served twelve years; the fetched page did not confirm it.

candidates.summary: Incumbent (listed by the district as Rich Gadacz) and the only candidate for the District 2 seat; listed on the state list as Nonpartisan {np_board}{in_list}.
background: New Prairie High School graduate (1982); studied business administration at Indiana University South Bend {np_board}.
Has worked mostly in building science and energy efficiency; Quality Assurance Manager at Solutions for Energy Efficiency Logistics {np_board}.
Parent of two New Prairie graduates {np_board}.
path_to_ballot: Was on the 2022 ballot for the District 2 seat as Richard L. Gadacz {lp_2022_galena1}.
Listed on the state list as Nonpartisan and is the only candidate for the seat {in_list}.
on_incumbent: In August 2026 he moved to suspend the regular meeting for the annual budget hearing, and thanked FFA staff for their presentation {np_n_260831}{np_n_260824}.
gaps: No campaign website, questionnaire, forum answers or news coverage of his 2026 campaign found.
